diagrams.title: From Account Signal to Earned Operator Revenue
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages connect research, outreach, acceptance, and billing.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Sequence numbers indicate workflow order, not conversion rates. The operator earns retainers and qualified-opportunity fees; client pipeline amounts and signed contract values remain outside operator revenue. Salesforce, HubSpot, and Calendly are example tools rather than required vendors.
diagrams.caption: Every invoice traces to delivered service or a documented acceptance event, not an inflated client pipeline valuation.

stages.label: Define the commercial unit
stages.value: Document scope, fee trigger, exclusions, and account ownership.
stages.detail: Specify the ideal customer profile, named-account territory, retainer deliverables, qualification rubric, attribution window, duplicate rules, and dispute timetable before outreach.

stages.label: Qualify account signals
stages.value: Attach source evidence and timestamps to each target account.
stages.detail: Combine public filings, client-supplied account history, and permitted data sources. Record company identity, business trigger, buying role, provenance, and suppression status.

stages.label: Orchestrate relevant outreach
stages.value: Coordinate account messaging, channel controls, and meeting availability.
stages.detail: Use HubSpot or Salesforce to manage contact ownership and suppression. Automate scheduling through Calendly only after checking timezone, seller capacity, and account-routing rules.

stages.label: Secure opportunity acceptance
stages.value: Obtain client confirmation against the written qualification rubric.
stages.detail: Capture the attended conversation, relevant buying role, documented business problem, agreed next step, and client acceptance timestamp. A booked calendar slot alone does not satisfy the illustrated qualified-opportunity standard.

stages.label: Recognize and reconcile fees
stages.value: Match earned retainers and accepted opportunities to invoice lines.
stages.detail: Reconcile the CRM acceptance ledger with invoices, credits, and collections. Resolve duplicate claims before billing; record advance payments separately until the contracted service has been delivered.

diagrams.title: A Single Cohort, Five Observable Outcomes
diagrams.subtitle: Track client-account pairs instead of mixing contacts, meetings, and deals.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative annual cohort across nine operator clients, followed through a full observation window. Each unit is one unique client-account pair, and each later stage is a subset of the preceding stage. Count at most one qualifying opportunity and one downstream win per pair. Counts are planning assumptions, not measured benchmarks. Downstream customer wins may occur after the opportunity-fee recognition period.
diagrams.caption: Base revenue bridge: nine clients paying $60,000 in earned annual retainers produce $540,000; 90 accepted opportunities at $1,500 produce $135,000; total operator revenue is $675,000.

stages.label: Eligible target pairs
stages.value: 2,400 client-account pairs enter the defined annual cohort.
stages.detail: Create stable client-account identifiers, verify account fit, and exclude suppression records and existing opportunities barred by the attribution agreement.

stages.label: Meaningfully engaged pairs
stages.value: 600 pairs engage; 25.0% of eligible target pairs.
stages.detail: Require a substantive response or documented buying interaction. Email delivery, tracking-pixel activity, and bot-generated clicks do not qualify as engagement.

stages.label: Attended discovery pairs
stages.value: 180 pairs attend discovery; 30.0% of engaged pairs.
stages.detail: Require an attended session with a relevant buying role. Reschedules and repeated meetings retain the same pair identifier and do not increase the cohort count.

stages.label: Accepted opportunity pairs
stages.value: 90 pairs qualify; 50.0% of attended discovery pairs.
stages.detail: Client acceptance must satisfy the contracted rubric and attribution rules. These 90 billable events support the $135,000 opportunity-fee component of the Base illustration.

stages.label: Client contract wins
stages.value: 18 pairs become customers; 20.0% of accepted opportunities.
stages.detail: Record downstream wins to evaluate delivery quality. The resulting customer contract values belong to clients and contribute zero additional operator revenue in this model.

diagrams.title: The $675,000 Base Revenue-to-Net Bridge
diagrams.subtitle: Four expense deductions leave $202,500, exactly 30.0% of revenue.
diagrams.assumptions_note: USD annual amounts. The first and final bars are absolute totals; the four intervening bars are signed expense changes. Expense categories are illustrative allocations, not supplied scorecard line items. Canonical Base costs total $472,500, or $39,375 per month, so the supplied $4,000–$20,000 monthly opex range cannot describe fully loaded Base expenses. This illustration assigns $5,625 monthly to operating overhead and separately budgets payroll, contractors, and direct delivery; that classification is an explicit modeling assumption.
diagrams.caption: $675,000 − $180,000 − $135,000 − $90,000 − $67,500 = $202,500. Canonical annual revenue, margin, and owner net: Conservative $150,000 / 20% / $30,000; Base $675,000 / 30.0% / $202,500; Scaled $1,200,000 / 40% / $480,000. Conservative and Base use five people; Scaled uses seven.

stages.label: Recognized operator revenue
stages.value: $675,000 earned from retainers and accepted-opportunity fees.
stages.detail: Opening absolute total: $540,000 of earned retainers plus $135,000 of accepted-opportunity fees. Exclude client contract values and unearned customer deposits.

stages.label: Full-time personnel
stages.value: Subtract $180,000 for the two full-time operator seats.
stages.detail: Illustrative loaded annual personnel budget for the operator lead and account director, including budgeted founder pay where applicable. Running balance: $495,000.

stages.label: Contract specialist delivery
stages.value: Subtract $135,000 for three contracted specialist seats.
stages.detail: Allocate contracted research, campaign production, and CRM operations costs to the core pod. Contract scope and worker classification require separate review. Running balance: $360,000.

stages.label: Direct campaign delivery
stages.value: Subtract $90,000 for operator-funded campaign delivery inputs.
stages.detail: Budget incremental campaign data, client-specific production, and other direct delivery inputs without duplicating contractor costs. Client-funded pass-through spend is excluded from this illustration. Running balance: $270,000.

stages.label: Operating overhead
stages.value: Subtract $67,500 for shared operating and administrative costs.
stages.detail: Budget shared CRM subscriptions, accounting, insurance, security administration, and payment processing separately from direct campaign inputs. Monthly equivalent: $5,625. Running balance: $202,500.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.value: $202,500 remaining equals the canonical 30.0% Base margin.
stages.detail: Closing absolute total, not another positive cash-flow increment. Divide $202,500 by $675,000 to obtain 30.0%; do not add budgeted founder pay back into this metric.

diagrams.title: Compare Contracted Fee Yield, Not Client Deal Size
diagrams.subtitle: Five illustrative enterprise sub-niches priced per accepted opportunity.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are illustrative USD operator fees per accepted opportunity, excluding retainers and before delivery expense. They are neither market quotations nor profit estimates. The five bars are alternative pricing hypotheses, not a portfolio mix to be added together. The Base illustration uses only the $1,500 fee assumption. ACH and wire describe collection methods, not permission to pay referral fees.
diagrams.caption: Test fee yield against delivery cost, acceptance rate, collection delay, and dispute frequency before choosing a sub-niche.

stages.label: Workforce software
stages.value: $900 per accepted enterprise workforce-software opportunity.
stages.detail: Illustrative ACH collection against a verified acceptance record. Qualify organization size, operating footprint, buying role, and a defined workforce-platform initiative.

stages.label: Logistics software
stages.value: $1,200 per accepted enterprise logistics-software opportunity.
stages.detail: Illustrative ACH collection for software demand generation, not freight brokerage. Qualify shipment scale, integration requirements, operations ownership, and an active evaluation.

stages.label: Industrial software
stages.value: $1,500 per accepted enterprise industrial-software opportunity.
stages.detail: Base fee assumption: 90 accepted opportunities generate $135,000. Qualify facility context, technical owner, integration constraints, and a documented evaluation step.

stages.label: Cybersecurity platforms
stages.value: $1,800 per accepted enterprise cybersecurity-platform opportunity.
stages.detail: Illustrative wire collection after documented acceptance. Qualify security ownership, deployment context, procurement path, and relevant need without collecting sensitive system access details.

stages.label: Enterprise data platforms
stages.value: $2,100 per accepted enterprise data-platform opportunity.
stages.detail: Illustrative wire collection against a fixed-fee invoice. Qualify architecture fit, data-platform ownership, migration trigger, and a credible next evaluation step; exclude any percentage of the client's contract value.

diagrams.title: Four Pre-Flight Decisions Before Outreach
diagrams.subtitle: Proceed on documented facts; remediate or exclude unsupported activities.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values indicate ordered decision nodes, not legal-risk scores. Each node has an explicit proceed branch and a remediation branch. Apply the cited federal rules together with relevant state requirements, contract terms, and the actual channel and sector. A business audience does not automatically remove privacy or outreach obligations.
diagrams.caption: A data license, an email address, or a flat-fee label alone does not establish that the proposed activity is permitted.

stages.label: Privacy and provenance
stages.value: Proceed with documented permitted use; otherwise quarantine records.
stages.detail: Evaluate California Civil Code 1798.100 and 1798.140 where applicable, including covered-business status, collection notices, purposes, and data relationships. Proceed when sourcing and use are supported; otherwise exclude the records until deficiencies are resolved.

stages.label: Commercial email controls
stages.value: Proceed with compliant sender controls; otherwise repair campaign setup.
stages.detail: Apply 15 U.S.C. 7704 to commercial email, including accurate headers, nondeceptive subjects, required identification, a valid postal address, and an opt-out mechanism. Honor opt-outs within ten business days. Proceed after checks pass; otherwise pause affected sends.

stages.label: Telephone and text permissions
stages.value: Proceed with channel-specific evidence; otherwise disable affected outreach.
stages.detail: Evaluate 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200 against number type, dialing technology, artificial or prerecorded voice use, purpose, consent requirements, calling times, and do-not-call duties. Proceed only for supported uses; otherwise remove calls or texts from the sequence.

stages.label: Sector and fee restrictions
stages.value: Proceed with permitted compensation; otherwise exclude or redesign scope.
stages.detail: Screen healthcare referrals under 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b(b), covered settlement-service referrals under 12 U.S.C. 2607, and federal procurement compensation under FAR 3.402 and 52.203-5 where applicable. Proceed only with supported fee terms and written attribution rules; otherwise exclude the activity or obtain a reviewed alternative.

diagrams.title: The Five-Person Core and Seven-Person Expansion
diagrams.subtitle: Two full-time seats plus three contractors; add one of each at scale.
diagrams.assumptions_note: FT means full-time; C means contractor. Numeric values show Base seat occupancy: five occupied seats and two expansion seats at zero. Conservative and Base use 2 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 3 FT + 4 C. Contractor seats represent people, not full-time equivalents. Role design is illustrative; contractor status depends on the actual working relationship.
diagrams.caption: The account director owns client acceptance; the CRM specialist maintains evidence; the operator lead resolves pricing, capacity, and customer-concentration decisions.

stages.label: Operator lead
stages.value: Core FT seat: own sales, pricing, capacity, and cash.
stages.detail: Maintain the agency sales pipeline, approve commercial terms, review client concentration monthly, and compare collections with payroll and contractor commitments.

stages.label: Account director
stages.value: Core FT seat: own client outcomes and acceptance quality.
stages.detail: Translate client strategy into account plans, run delivery reviews, secure opportunity acceptance, and resolve scope issues before they become attribution disputes.

stages.label: Account research specialist
stages.value: Core C seat: own target research and signal qualification.
stages.detail: Produce sourced account briefs, maintain identity matching, check suppression records, and flag weak buying signals before campaign production consumes delivery capacity.

stages.label: Campaign production specialist
stages.value: Core C seat: own messaging assets and outreach preparation.
stages.detail: Develop account-relevant messaging, prepare channel-specific campaign assets, inspect suppression settings, and route substantive replies into the client-account record.

stages.label: CRM and attribution specialist
stages.value: Core C seat: own scheduling, acceptance evidence, and reconciliation.
stages.detail: Configure Salesforce or HubSpot workflows, connect Calendly routing, preserve source timestamps, deduplicate events, and reconcile accepted opportunities with invoice lines.

stages.label: Client success manager
stages.value: Expansion FT seat: activate for the seven-person Scaled pod.
stages.detail: Add one full-time person to absorb onboarding, reporting, and renewal coordination when measured account workload exceeds the core account director's sustainable capacity.

stages.label: Research and production support
stages.value: Expansion C seat: activate for the seven-person Scaled pod.
stages.detail: Add one contracted specialist for the demonstrated research or production bottleneck. Preserve qualification standards rather than increasing volume through weaker acceptance criteria.

diagrams.title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Expanding Delivery
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets sum to a $60,000 illustrative launch budget.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are USD allocations in the $60,000 central illustration, inside the canonical $15,000–$100,000 startup range. Allocation shares are 20%, 30%, 20%, and 30%. Applying the same shares to the two endpoints produces complete $15,000 and $100,000 comparison budgets. These are cash allocations, not annual expenses or recognized revenue.
diagrams.caption: First-deal timing remains 3–12 months. The $18,000 reserve covers 4.5 months at $4,000 monthly cash burn or 0.9 months at $20,000; it does not fund a fully staffed Base pod.

stages.label: Formation and operating setup
stages.value: $12,000 central allocation; 20% of total startup capital.
stages.detail: Fund entity setup, contract drafting, initial insurance, security configuration, and bookkeeping implementation. At the $15,000 and $100,000 endpoints, allocate $3,000 and $20,000 respectively.

stages.label: CRM and research infrastructure
stages.value: $18,000 central allocation; 30% of total startup capital.
stages.detail: Fund scoped CRM implementation, licensed research inputs, scheduling integration, and initial attribution reporting. At the $15,000 and $100,000 endpoints, allocate $4,500 and $30,000 respectively.

stages.label: Pilot production and proof
stages.value: $12,000 central allocation; 20% of total startup capital.
stages.detail: Fund limited specialist assignments, account briefs, messaging assets, and acceptance-ledger testing for a narrow pilot. At the $15,000 and $100,000 endpoints, allocate $3,000 and $20,000 respectively.

stages.label: Uncommitted cash reserve
stages.value: $18,000 central allocation; 30% of total startup capital.
stages.detail: Retain liquid cash for collection delays and essential operating commitments. At the $15,000 and $100,000 endpoints, allocate $4,500 and $30,000 respectively. Reduce commitments or secure more runway if the sales-cycle forecast exceeds available cash.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to an Instrumented Pilot
diagrams.subtitle: Build operating evidence now; allow 3–12 months for the first deal.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values mark milestone end days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. The sprint establishes a functioning pilot and decision evidence, not a promised signed client or enterprise contract. Outreach requires the relevant checks to be completed and, when acting for a client, documented client authorization.
diagrams.caption: Finish with traceable account records, tested acceptance logic, a reconciled pilot ledger, and a cash-backed continuation decision.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.value: Select one sub-niche and define the billable opportunity.
stages.detail: Interview prospective buyers, document the ideal customer profile, define retainer deliverables and acceptance criteria, review sector restrictions, and build a cash forecast around the 3–12 month first-deal range.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.value: Configure the CRM, provenance records, and suppression workflows.
stages.detail: Implement client-account identifiers, source timestamps, contact restrictions, acceptance fields, and invoice references. Test scheduling, duplicate detection, opt-out handling, and access controls using clearly labeled test records.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.value: Run a narrow pilot with documented outreach authority.
stages.detail: Launch a capacity-limited account cohort only after pre-flight checks. If no client is signed, test the agency's own acquisition workflow instead of claiming client delivery. Record replies, attended meetings, labor hours, and actual cash spend.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.value: Audit cohort evidence and decide the next funded iteration.
stages.detail: Review acceptance failures, duplicate claims, response quality, collection terms, and client concentration exposure. Reconcile any earned fees with the ledger, update the cash forecast, and expand only when workload and available runway support the added commitments.
